source_text: –Εἴρηται πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ἃ εἴρηται· οἱ ἄτεκνοι τίνα ἡμῖν εὐπρόσωπον αἰτίαν τῆς φειδωλίας προβάλλονται; Οὐ πωλῶ τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, οὐδὲ δίδωμι τοῖς πτωχοῖς, διὰ τὰς ἀναγκαίας τοῦ βίου χρείας. Οὐκοῦν οὐχ ὁ Κύριός σου διδάσκαλος, οὐδὲ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον ῥυθμίζει σου τὸν βίον, ἀλλ' αὐτὸς σὺ νομοθετεῖς σεαυτῷ. Βλέπε δὲ εἰς οἷον κίνδυνον ἐμπίπτεις οὕτω διανοούμενος. Εἰ γὰρ ὁ μὲν Κύριος ὡς ἀναγκαῖα ἡμῖν διετάξατο, σὺ δὲ ὡς ἀδύνατα παραγράφῃ, οὐδὲν ἕτερον ἢ φρονιμώτερον σεαυτὸν εἶναι λέγεις τοῦ νομοθέτου. Ἀλλ' ἀπολαύσας αὐτῶν παρὰ πᾶσάν μου τὴν ζωὴν, μετὰ τὴν τελευτὴν τοῦ βίου διαδόχους ποιήσομαι τῶν ἐμοὶ προσόντων τοὺς πένη τας, γράμμασι καὶ διαθήκαις κυρίους αὐτοὺς τῶν ἐμῶν ἀποδείξας. Ὅτε οὐκέτι ἔσῃ ἐν ἀνθρώποις, τότε γενήσῃ φιλάνθρωπος· ὅταν νεκρόν σε ἴδω, τότε σε εἴπω φιλάδελφον. Πολλή σοι χάρις τῆς φιλοτιμίας, ὅτι ἐν τῷ μνήματι κείμενος, καὶ εἰς γῆν διαλυθεὶς, ἁδρὸς γέγονας ταῖς δαπάναις καὶ μεγαλόψυχος. Ποίων, εἰπέ μοι, καιρῶν τοὺς μισθοὺς ἀπαιτήσεις, τῶν ἐν τῇ ζωῇ, ἢ τῶν μετὰ τὴν ἀποβίωσιν; Ἀλλ' ὃν μὲν ἔζης χρόνον, καθηδυπαθῶν τοῦ βίου καὶ τῇ τρυφῇ διαῤῥέων, οὐδὲ προσβλέπειν ἠνείχου τοὺς πένητας· ἀποθανόντος δὲ ποία μὲν πρᾶξις; ποῖος δὲ μισθὸς ἐργασίας ὀφεί λεται; Δεῖξον τὰ ἔργα, καὶ ἀπαίτει τὰς ἀντιδόσεις. Οὐδεὶς μετὰ τὸ λυθῆναι τὴν πανήγυριν πραγματεύεται· οὐδὲ μετὰ τοὺς ἀγῶνας ἐπελθὼν στεφανοῦ ται· οὐδὲ μετὰ τοὺς πολέμους ἀνδραγαθίζεται· οὐ τοίνυν οὐδὲ μετὰ τὴν ζωὴν εὐσεβεῖ δηλονότι. Ἐν μέλανι καὶ γράμμασι κατεπαγγέλλῃ τὰς εὐποιίας. Τίς οὖν ἀναγγελεῖ σοι τὸν καιρὸν τῆς ἐξόδου; τίς ἐγγυητὴς ἔσται τοῦ τρόπου τῆς τελευτῆς; Πόσοι ὑπὸ βιαίων ἀνηρπάσθησαν συμπτωμάτων, οὐδὲ φωνὴν ῥῆξαι συγχωρηθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ πάθους; Πόσους πυρετὸς ἐποίησεν ἔκφρονας; Τί οὖν ἀναμένεις καιρὸν, ἐν ᾧ πολλάκις οὐδὲ τῶν λογισμῶν τῶν σεαυτοῦ ἔσῃ κύριος; Νὺξ βαθεῖα, καὶ νόσος βαρεῖα, καὶ ὁ βοηθῶν οὐδαμοῦ· καὶ ὁ ἐφεδρεύων τῷ κλήρῳ ἕτοιμος, πάντα πρὸς τὸ ἑαυτοῦ χρήσιμον διοικούμενος, ἄπρακτά σοι ποιῶν τὰ βουλεύματα. Εἶτα περιβλεψάμενος ὧδε καὶ ὧδε, καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν περιεστῶσάν σε ἐρημίαν, τότε αἰσθήσῃ τῆς ἀβουλίας· τότε στενάξεις τὴν ἄνοιαν, εἰς οἷον καιρὸν ἐταμιεύου τὴν ἐντολὴν, ὅτε ἡ μὲν γλῶσσα παρεῖται, ἡ δὲ χεὶρ ὑπότρομος ἤδη κλονουμένη ταῖς συνολκαῖς, ὡς μήτε φωνῇ μήτε γράμματι διασημάναι τὴν γνώμην. Καίτοι εἰ καὶ πάντα φανερῶς ἐγέγραπτο, καὶ πᾶσα φωνὴ διαῤῥήδην κεκήρυκτο, ἓν γράμμα παρεντεθὲν ἱκανὸν ἦν πᾶσαν μεταποιῆσαι τὴν γνώμην· μία σφραγὶς παραποιηθεῖσα, δύο ἢ τρεῖς μάρτυρες ἄδικοι, ὅλον ἂν τὸν κλῆρον ἐφ' ἑτέρους μετήνεγκαν.
orientation: Basil is addressing the rich who put off giving until after death, and now he turns to their excuse that they must keep their possessions for life's necessities.
pass_a_gloss: What has been said to fathers has been said. The childless, what plausible excuse for stinginess do they put forward to us? "I do not sell my possessions, nor do I give to the poor, because of the necessary needs of life." Therefore the Lord is not your teacher, nor does the Gospel order your life, but you yourself legislate for yourself. But see into what kind of danger you fall by thinking this way. For if the Lord commanded these things to us as necessary, but you write them off as impossible, you say nothing other than that you are wiser than the lawgiver. "But after enjoying them through all my life, after the end of life I will make the poor heirs of what belongs to me, by letters and wills declaring them lords of my property." When you are no longer among human beings, then you will become a lover of humanity; when I see you a corpse, then I will call you a lover of your brother. Much thanks to you for your generosity, that lying in the tomb and dissolved into earth, you have become lavish in expenditures and great-souled. For what times, tell me, will you demand the wages—for the times in life, or for the times after death? But during the time you were living, luxuriating in life and flowing with softness, you could not bear even to look at the poor; but when you have died, what action is there? What wage for work is owed? Show the deeds, and demand the returns. No one does business after the festival has broken up; nor does one who arrives after the contests receive a crown; nor does one play the hero after the wars; so clearly neither does one act piously after life. In ink and letters you promise the good deeds. Who then will announce to you the time of your departure? Who will be guarantor of the manner of your death? How many were snatched away by violent misfortunes, not even permitted to utter a sound because of the suffering? How many did fever make out of their minds? Why then do you wait for a time in which often you will not even be master of your own thoughts? Deep night, and heavy illness, and the helper nowhere; and the one lying in wait for the inheritance is ready, arranging everything for his own advantage, making your plans ineffective. Then looking around here and there, and seeing the desolation surrounding you, then you will perceive your folly; then you will groan at your foolishness, at what a time you were storing up the commandment, when the tongue is paralyzed, and the hand already trembling, shaken by convulsions, so that neither by voice nor by writing can you make known your intention. And yet even if everything had been written clearly, and every word had been proclaimed expressly, one inserted letter was enough to alter the whole intention; one forged seal, two or three unjust witnesses, would have transferred the whole inheritance to others.

lemmas.gloss: flowing with softness, dissolving in luxury
play the hero, perform brave deeds

choices.why: The noun names the vice of withholding surplus from the poor; 'stinginess' keeps the moral force and avoids the glossary-banned 'avarice'.
εὐπρόσωπος means 'fair-faced' or 'specious'; 'plausible excuse' captures the rhetorical force of an objection that looks good but is false.
παραγράφω is a legal term for striking out or rejecting a clause; 'write off' preserves the metaphor of invalidating the Lord's command as if it were a legal document.
The compound is deliberately parallel to φιλάδελφος; rendering both as 'lover of...' keeps Basil's sarcastic pairing visible.
The verb means 'living in pleasure'; 'luxuriating' conveys the self-indulgent softness Basil condemns, and pairs with 'flowing with softness' for διαρρέων.

choices.english: lying in wait for the inheritance
choices.why: ἐφεδρεύω is a military term for lying in ambush; 'lying in wait' keeps the predatory image of heirs circling the dying rich man.

pass_b_english: What has been said to fathers has been said. But what plausible excuse for stinginess do the childless put forward to us? "I am not selling my possessions, and I am not giving to the poor, because of the necessary needs of life." So then the Lord is not your teacher, and the Gospel does not order your life—you make laws for yourself. But see what danger you fall into by thinking this way. For if the Lord commanded these things as necessary for us, and you write them off as impossible, you are saying nothing other than that you are wiser than the lawgiver.

"But after enjoying them all my life long, after the end of my life I will make the poor heirs of what belongs to me, proving them owners of my property by documents and wills." When you are no longer among human beings, then you will become a lover of humanity; when I see you a corpse, then I will call you a lover of your brother. Many thanks to you for your generosity—that lying in the tomb and dissolved into earth, you have become lavish in your spending and great-souled.

Tell me, for which season will you demand the rewards—those in life, or those after death? But during the time you lived, luxuriating in life and flowing with softness, you could not bear even to look at the poor. And once you are dead, what action is there? What wage is owed for work? Show the deeds, and demand the returns. No one does business after the festival has broken up; no one is crowned after arriving when the contests are over; no one plays the hero after the wars are done. So clearly no one practices piety after life either.

In ink and letters you promise your good deeds. Who then will announce to you the hour of your departure? Who will guarantee the manner of your death? How many have been snatched away by violent misfortunes, not even permitted by their suffering to utter a sound? How many has fever driven out of their minds? Why then do you wait for a time when you will often not even be master of your own thoughts?

Deep night, and heavy sickness, and no one anywhere to help; and the one lying in wait for the inheritance is ready, arranging everything for his own advantage and making your plans useless. Then, looking around this way and that and seeing the desolation surrounding you, you will at last perceive your folly; then you will groan at your foolishness—at what a time you stored up the commandment, when your tongue is paralyzed and your hand is already trembling, shaken by convulsions, so that neither by voice nor by writing can you make your intention known.

And yet even if everything had been written clearly and every word had been proclaimed aloud, one inserted letter was enough to alter the whole intention; one forged seal, two or three unjust witnesses, could have transferred the entire inheritance to others.

last_rejected.quote: could have transferred the entire inheritance to others
last_rejected.source_quote: δύο ἢ τρεῖς μάρτυρες ἄδικοι, ὅλον ἂν τὸν κλῆρον μετήνεγκαν
last_rejected.why: Subject is the witnesses, not the seal; witnesses could transfer the inheritance.
last_rejected.fix: one forged seal, or two or three unjust witnesses, could have transferred the entire inheritance to others
last_rejected.ruling: ἐφ' ἑτέρους μετήνεγκαν has no expressed subject; Greek often omits subject when clear from participial clause (σφραγὶς παραποιηθεῖσα). English 'could have transferred' with compound subject is acceptable rendering.

last_rejected.why: τρυφῇ means luxury/delight, not softness; διαῤῥέων suggests dissolving/wasting away in luxury
last_rejected.fix: dissolving in luxury or wasting away in indulgence
last_rejected.ruling: τρυφῇ covers luxury/softness/delicate living; 'flowing with softness' captures διαῤῥέων adequately within range.

last_rejected.why: καιρῶν here means times/opportunities, not seasons; asks which period's rewards
last_rejected.ruling: καιρῶν includes 'season' as a normal sense; context makes 'which period' clear to readers.

last_rejected.why: ἀνδραγαθίζεται means acts bravely/does noble deeds, not 'plays the hero' which sounds performative/mock-heroic
last_rejected.fix: does brave deeds or wins honor
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνδραγαθίζεται means act bravely; 'plays the hero' is idiomatic English within the word's range.

last_rejected.why: παρεντεθὲν means interpolated/inserted fraudulently, but 'inserted' alone misses the sense of tampering; context is forgery
last_rejected.fix: one letter interpolated or one letter fraudulently inserted
last_rejected.ruling: παρεντεθὲν means inserted/interpolated; 'inserted' is accurate, and context of forgery is clear from surrounding text.

last_rejected.why: παραποιηθεῖσα means altered/counterfeited, not specifically 'forged'; seal could be tampered with in various ways
last_rejected.fix: one seal counterfeited or one seal altered
last_rejected.ruling: παραποιηθεῖσα means altered/tampered; 'forged seal' is a natural English rendering within the word's range.
